title: Criterion for a scheme colimit to have algebraic-space targets
statement: Let $B$ be a scheme and $J$ a small category in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $(X_j)_{j\in J}$ be a diagram of $B$-schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $(X,X_j\to X)$ be a colimit cocone in $B$-schemes, meaning that maps $X\to Z$ correspond to compatible families $X_j\to Z$ for every $B$-scheme $Z$. Assume (i) the maps $X_j\to X$ are jointly surjective; (ii) for every etale scheme $V\to X$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], its base changes $V_j=V\times_X X_j$ have colimit $V$ in $B$-schemes [def-pc-fibre-product]; and (iii) every compatible family of etale schemes $V_j\to X_j$ with separated structure maps is obtained by base change from an etale scheme $V\to X$. Compatibility means an isomorphism $V_j\simeq V_k\times_{X_k}X_j$ for every arrow $j\to k$, respecting identities and composition; separated means that the relative diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then the same cocone is a colimit in algebraic spaces over $B$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]: maps $X\to Q$ correspond bijectively to compatible families $X_j\to Q$ for every algebraic space $Q/B$.

source.place: Tag 07SX, lemma-colimit-agrees, with the finite span diagram as the application in Tag 07SY.

proof.text: Fix an algebraic space $Q/B$ and compatible maps $f_j:X_j\to Q$. By [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover] choose a surjective etale atlas $w:W\to Q$ with $W=\coprod_a W_a$ and each $W_a$ affine. This atlas is separated; here are the details needed to apply (iii). The summands are disjoint open and closed subschemes by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-separated-affine-cover-criterion] to $W\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$: for distinct summands their intersection is the empty affine scheme and its ring is zero; for a summand with ring $A$, the required multiplication $A\otimes_{\mathbf Z}A\to A$ is surjective since $a$ is the image of $a\otimes1$. Thus the absolute diagonal of $W$ is a closed immersion. The square with top arrow $\Delta_w:W\to W\times_QW$, bottom arrow the absolute diagonal $W\to W\times_{\mathbf Z}W$, and left arrow the identity, is cartesian: on every scheme test, two identical $W$-sections automatically have the same $Q$-image. Consequently $\Delta_w$ is a closed immersion, being a base change of the closed immersion $W\to W\times_{\mathbf Z}W$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. By the same lemma, for every scheme $T$ with a map $T\to W\times_QW$ the base change $T\times_{W\times_QW}W\to T$ of $\Delta_w$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]; thus the diagonal of $w$ is a representable closed immersion, i.e. $w$ is separated. All the fibre products with two scheme sources over $Q$ are schemes by its representable diagonal [def-trf-algebraic-space].

Put $U_j=X_j\times_{Q,f_j}W$ and let $h_j:U_j\to W$ be the second projection. These are schemes and their maps to $X_j$ are surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]; they are separated by base change of $w$, using [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition]. For an arrow $j\to k$, a pair $(x_j,z)$ maps to $(x_k,z)$, giving $U_j\simeq X_j\times_{X_k}U_k$; these identifications satisfy identities and composition because both coordinates do. Hence (iii) supplies an etale scheme $p:U\to X$ and coherent identifications $U\times_X X_j\simeq U_j$. The $h_j$ form a compatible family of $B$-scheme maps. By (ii) applied to $U\to X$ there is a unique $B$-scheme map $h:U\to W$ restricting to all $h_j$.

Let $D=U\times_XU$, with projections $p_1,p_2$, and $D_j=U_j\times_{X_j}U_j$. Etale base change and composition [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties] show that $D\to X$ is etale. Its base change to $X_j$ is $D_j$, by the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. Thus (ii) makes $D$ the colimit of the $D_j$ in $B$-schemes. Put $R=W\times_QW$, a scheme by the representable diagonal of $Q$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. On $D_j$ the two maps $h_j\operatorname{pr}_1,h_j\operatorname{pr}_2$ have the same $Q$-image, namely $f_j$ composed with the structure map to $X_j$, so they define a compatible family $r_j:D_j\to R$. The scheme-colimit property produces $r:D\to R$. Its composite with $R\to W\times_BW$ equals $(hp_1,hp_2)$: both have the same restrictions to every $D_j$, and the target is a $B$-scheme. Therefore $whp_1=whp_2$.

The map $p:U\to X$ is surjective. Indeed, for $x\in X$, (i) supplies $j$ and $x_j\in X_j$ mapping to $x$; surjectivity of $U_j\to X_j$ supplies $u_j$ above $x_j$, whose image in $U$ maps to $x$. Since $p$ is etale, it is flat and locally of finite presentation [def-weil-etale-morphism], so $\{p\}$ is an fppf covering [def-pc-fppf-site]. The algebraic space $Q$ is an fppf sheaf [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Its sheaf equalizer [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] for this covering, together with the equality on $D$ just proved, gives a unique section $f\in Q(X)$ restricting to $wh\in Q(U)$. A section of $Q$ on a scheme $T$ is the same as a morphism $h_T\to Q$: its value on a map $a:T'\to T$ is the restriction of the section along $a$, and conversely a natural transformation is determined by its value on $\mathrm{id}_T$. Thus $f$ is a $B$-morphism $X\to Q$. For every $j$, both $f|_{X_j}$ and $f_j$ restrict on the surjective etale map $U_j\to X_j$ to $wh_j$. Applying the same sheaf equalizer on $X_j$ gives $f|_{X_j}=f_j$.

To prove uniqueness, suppose $f,g:X\to Q$ have equal restrictions on every $X_j$. Pull back the atlas $W\to Q$ separately along $f$ and $g$ to get surjective etale schemes $A\to X$ and $C\to X$, with lifts $a:A\to W$ and $c:C\to W$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The scheme $T=A\times_X C$ is surjective etale over $X$: its projection to $A$ is a base change of the covering $C\to X$, and the composite of two surjective etale maps is surjective etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-composition]. Apply (ii) to $T\to X$, so $T$ is the colimit of $T_j=T\times_X X_j$. The pair of lifts $(a\operatorname{pr}_A,c\operatorname{pr}_C):T\to W\times_BW$ factors on each $T_j$ through the scheme $R=W\times_QW$, because $f|_{X_j}=g|_{X_j}$. These maps to $R$ are compatible by their two projections. The colimit of the $T_j$ gives $T\to R$, and uniqueness for the scheme target $W\times_BW$ identifies its composite with that pair of lifts. Hence $f|_T=g|_T$. The etale covering $T\to X$ is fppf by [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-pc-fppf-site], and the sheaf equalizer [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] for $Q$ implies $f=g$.

Restriction along the given cocone always sends a map $X\to Q$ to a compatible family. Step 4 proves that every compatible family is its restriction, and step 5 proves injectivity. This is the required bijection for every algebraic space $Q/B$, hence the claimed colimit universal property.

tool_uses.why: The arbitrary algebraic-space atlas from a disjoint union of affines is the generic input to the first sentence of Tag 07SX; no specialized finiteness or curve statement replaces it.
Only the disjoint open-and-closed affine summands of an atlas are used to check its separatedness.
The separated affine-cover criterion is applied over Spec Z to the affine summands of an atlas, with empty or identical intersections.
Only formation of scheme pullbacks of an etale atlas and stability of surjective etale covers under base change are used, as generic tools in Tag 07SX.
The composite of the two surjective etale projections in the uniqueness cover is surjective etale; this is a generic covering calculation.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NF-4f36ebb5e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the Stacks source, Tag 07SX (spaces-pushouts.tex lines 116-163). The item statement matches it hypothesis by hypothesis. The one change is that the item takes its colimits in B-schemes, where Stacks takes them in all schemes. That makes the item's hypotheses weaker for the same conclusion, and every target the proof uses is over B (W, W x_B W, R = W x_Q W), so the item is still proved. It still covers the Tag 07SY application. There are no new nodes. The statement is identical to live, where the item is still unsplit, so no other group has superseded it. Changing blueprint.from.node to det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-direct-images is consistent with the via chain. Steps 2-6 are correct as written. Step 2: atlas pullbacks via lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers and separated base change in the spaces sense. Step 3: D->X is étale by the etale-source-target clauses (i)/(ii), and the factorization through R uses uniqueness for the target W x_B W. Step 4: the single map U->X is surjective, so it is an fppf covering, and the sheaf equalizer gives existence; recovering f_j uses the cover U_j->X_j. Step 5: the double-atlas T = A x_X C is a surjective étale cover via base change and lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-composition, which gives uniqueness. Edge cases with empty J or empty W work. FIX (C1/C4) in step 1: it took base-change stability of closed immersions from def-weil-closed-immersion, which does not state it, and it stopped at 'Delta_w is a closed immersion', while step 2 needs every scheme test of the diagonal to be one. Step 1 now cites the existing Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change (Tag 01QR) for both base changes and concludes that w is separated in the representable sense. The node is also added to proof_deps.
